notes.meaning: David speaks of the Lord as his personal shepherd who gently watches over him like a sheep. Because the Almighty God cares for him, he knows he will not lack anything that is truly good for his body or soul. Trusting in the Lord frees believers from the anxious fear of being left without help.

A faithful shepherd guides his sheep to soft, lush grass so they can rest safely and fully satisfied. He leads them to quiet, gentle waters where they can drink without being frightened by noisy, rushing streams. In the same way, God provides His people with peaceful rest and refreshing spiritual care.

When the sheep wanders or grows weary, the Shepherd brings it back and gives it new life and strength. God leads His people into right and holy ways of living, keeping them on the proper path. He does all this to honor His own name and show His faithful character.

Even when walking through dark, dangerous valleys or facing death itself, the believer does not need to be afraid. The Shepherd is right beside him, giving comfort through His close presence. His rod protects against attacking enemies, while His staff gently guides and supports the sheep.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars translate the phrase as a "valley of deep darkness," seeing it as a poetic picture of any dangerous ravine or severe trial rather than strictly physical death.

notes.meaning: The picture changes from a pasture to a rich banquet where God welcomes His servant as an honored guest. Even though enemies look on, they are completely powerless to stop God from spreading a table of abundant food and pouring fragrant oil of joy on his head. The overflowing cup shows that the Lord supplies far more than enough blessings for His people.

Because of God's past care, David is certain that divine kindness and unfailing love will pursue him every day of his life. He knows he will not be abandoned, but will live in loving fellowship with the Lord continually. This brings lasting hope of dwelling in God's presence here on earth and forever in His heavenly home.
